chunks: 5468 - As for the hadith of ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Thaʿlabah, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAmr ibn Shaddād al-Azdī, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A man has the greatest right over his wealth so long as the soul remains in him. If he bequeaths all of it, then it is permissible for him.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِمَالِهِ: having the strongest claim and authority over one’s own property
key_terms.أَوْصَى بِهِ: he made a bequest concerning it
key_terms.مَا دَامَ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ: so long as life remains in him

ai.seo_question: Does a person have the right to bequeath all of his wealth while still alive?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that a person retains authority over his property for as long as he remains alive. It indicates that if he makes a bequest concerning the whole of his wealth, that bequest is valid for him according to the wording of the narration.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5468 - As for the narration of Ali ibn Asbaṭ from Thaʿlabah from Abu Al-Hasan Amr ibn Shaddad Al-Azdi from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"A man has the most right over his wealth as long as his soul remains in him. If he bequeaths all of it, it is permissible for him."
